name: Curt Hennig Memorial Show

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Michael Manson pinned Matt Manning with the Sweet Dreams Stunner after Manning had come close to an upset with a top-rope gordbuster that Manson broke up with a foot on the ropes.
matches.stipulation: First round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title

matches.finish: Kazuo Shizaki pinned Richard Gideon after Gideon, who had attacked Shizaki's left knee before the bell, held the Final Judgment on him while the referee was out, and Shizaki's manager Jeriko knocked Gideon cold with a metal briefcase, laid Shizaki on top of him and woke the referee for the count.
matches.stipulation: First round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title

matches.finish: Beau Michaels pinned Aitsu Sugawara with the Running Crotchslam after a swinging neckbreaker and an Asai moonsault.
matches.stipulation: First round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title

matches.finish: Rat Fink advanced by forfeit because Bobby Lee could not make his flight through snow.
matches.stipulation: First round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title

matches.finish: Mike McGee won when Andre Eian passed out in the Pink Slip camel clutch and the referee called for the bell.
matches.stipulation: First round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title

matches.finish: Shawn Hart pinned Johnny Starr with his second Hart Attack (a Diamond Cutter).
matches.stipulation: First round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title

matches.finish: Doc Silver pinned Psycho with the Aces Full after kicking him low while the referee was down.
matches.stipulation: First round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title (main event)

notes: The fed's debut broadcast, a tribute to Curt Hennig and the first round of its tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title, posted in seven parts on 26 and 27 February 2003; the lineup post and the members' promos are on the wing's roleplay pages.

name: Almost Live

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Doc Silver pinned Rat Fink with the Aces Full after landing on his feet out of a Crucifix Powerbomb.
matches.stipulation: Second round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title

matches.finish: Shawn Hart pinned Mike McGee with the El Codo Explosivo after McGee had kicked out of a Hart Attack.
matches.stipulation: Second round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title

matches.finish: Michael Manson made Kazuo Shizaki submit to the Tourniquet after Shizaki had pinned Beau Michaels with an Asai moonsault; Michaels had been knocked out by a brick hidden in a book in the hands of Scotty Michaels, who made his first appearance in the fed.
matches.stipulation: Three-way elimination, second round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title (main event)

notes: The semi-final round of the tournament for the first WFW World Heavyweight Title, in which seven men became three. Its introduction, which announces the signing of a former CSWA world champion, is held on the CSWA wing (/promotions/cswa/rp/almost-live-introduction-cswa-champion-signs-2003-03-14.html).

name: Vox Hiberionacum

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Richard Gideon won the Cup, eliminating Rat Fink last by holding him in a gorilla press and dumping him over the top rope; Chris Bradford had gone out to Gideon, and Psycho and Scotty Michaels had gone over together.
matches.stipulation: Vox Hiberionacum Cup Royal Rumble: elimination by going over the top rope; the winner earns the first shot at the new World Heavyweight Champion

matches.finish: Doc Silver pinned Shawn Hart after Michael Manson, whose legs were being held from under the ring, could not break up the fall, and became the first WFW World Heavyweight Champion; Manson, who was not pinned, became the first North American Champion.
matches.stipulation: Three-way for the vacant WFW World Heavyweight Title; the man who was not pinned won the vacant WFW North American Title
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: The final of the tournament, held outdoors in the rain, which crowned the first WFW World Heavyweight Champion and North American Champion, with the Vox Hiberionacum Cup battle royal for the first shot at the new champion. The opening commentary says the two titles resume and carry on the lineage of the old NGEN World Heavyweight Title.

name: Shock & Awe

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Diablo won on his debut: Silly Simon pinned Bobby Lee, Diablo pinned Matt Manning with the Devil's Ragdoll and won a ten count over Aitsu Sugawara, then made Silly Simon tap to the Dragon Sleeper after a DDT when Simon had offered a draw.
matches.stipulation: Bunkhouse Brawl elimination match

matches.finish: Johnny Starr and Chris Bradford won two falls to one: Luster and Andre Eian took the first when the other team was disqualified after Luster faked being hit low, Bradford pinned Eian with an inside cradle for the second, and Bradford pinned him again with a small-package reversal for the third.
matches.stipulation: Best two out of three falls

matches.finish: Scotty Michaels pinned Mike McGee with a brainbuster after a flying forearm.
matches.stipulation: Number-one contender match for the North American Title

matches.finish: Richard Gideon pinned World Champion Doc Silver with the System Failure, a 450 into a frog splash, after Psycho's Tiger Driver 91 had taken Silver out.
matches.stipulation: Falls count anywhere tag team match (Doc Silver was World Champion; the title was not on the line)

notes: The fed's first non-tournament show, posted in eight parts: Diablo's debut, a two-out-of-three-falls tag match, the number-one-contender match for the North American Title, a falls-count-anywhere tag match in which the World Champion was pinned, and a Boot Camp title match that never started.

name: Gates of Hell

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Chris McMillan pinned Aitsu Sugawara with the Dread Driver (a Tiger Driver 91) in his WFW debut.
matches.stipulation: Debut of Chris McMillan

matches.finish: The thirty-minute limit expired as Psycho's Psycho Flight Stardust Press covered Shawn Hart; management ruled that both men would challenge for the title at the pay-per-view.
matches.stipulation: Number-one contender match for the WFW World Heavyweight Title, thirty-minute time limit

matches.finish: Johnny Starr pinned Chris Bradford with the Spotlight Razor's Edge after catching him on the top rope.
matches.stipulation: Qualifying match for the North American Title number-one contender match

matches.finish: Andre Eian pinned Luster with a Shadow Driver implant DDT after blinding him with a fireball while Chris Bradford distracted the referee.
matches.stipulation: Qualifying match for the North American Title number-one contender match

matches.finish: Scotty Michaels pinned Diablo with a small package after a brainbuster suplex; Rat Fink had broken up Diablo's pin and Manson had hit Diablo with a chair meant for Fink. The result put Michaels, Manson and Rat Fink in a ladder match for the North American Title.
matches.stipulation: Ultimate Jeopardy tag team match; the winning team decided the North American Title match at the pay-per-view

matches.finish: Both men were counted out after brawling through the crowd, so Doc Silver retained; management then added Gideon to the pay-per-view title match.
matches.stipulation: WFW World Heavyweight Title match (champion Doc Silver)
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: Posted in seven parts. Shock & Awe had announced the card for the Hammerstein Ballroom in New York; the broadcast itself opens live from Atlanta. It set up the fed's first pay-per-view.

name: Cherry Blossom Chaos

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

venue: the National Mall, by the Reflecting Pool

matches.finish: Luster pinned Chris Bradford with the Funk & Wagnall powerbomb.
Diablo pinned Chris McMillan with the Devil's Ragdoll Cobra Clutch Bomb; Shawn Hart then joined Diablo in beating McMillan down until Richard Gideon and Luster ran in with chairs.
Andre Eian pinned Johnny Starr with a Shadow Driver DDT from the top rope while Starr's foot was on the ropes; referee Mike McGee counted three without seeing it.
matches.stipulation: Number-one contender match for the North American Title, Mike McGee refereeing

matches.finish: Michael Manson, whose leg had been injured by a masked attacker earlier in the night, reclaimed the title by climbing the ladder and punching Rat Fink off it, after shackling Scotty Michaels to a ladder; video shown afterward revealed Michaels as the masked man.
matches.stipulation: Three-way ladder match for the North American Title
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american

matches.finish: Doc Silver was eliminated first when Shawn Hart dropped a leg on his head while Gideon held him in a leglock; Hart then eliminated Gideon with the Hart Attack, and Psycho pinned Hart with the Tiger Driver, after Silver struck Hart with a steel chair at the Lincoln Memorial, to become champion.
matches.stipulation: Four-way elimination for the WFW World Heavyweight Title, falls count anywhere, no countouts, on the Mall (main event)
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: The fed's first pay-per-view, a free show staged outdoors on the National Mall; every promo for the card was cut from a Washington location. It crowned Psycho World Heavyweight Champion.

name: Rage in the Cage

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Diablo pinned Luster with the Devil's Ragdoll Cobra Clutch Bomb after two DDTs.
Rat Fink pinned Chris McMillan with a side slam after his robot manager distracted McMillan.

Scotty Michaels pinned Michael Manson with a brainbuster suplex after Eian's Shadow Driver had put Manson down and Michaels had speared Eian; Felix Red, making his debut, fell a count short of the save.
matches.stipulation: Tag team match; Felix Red's debut

matches.finish: Shawn Hart pinned Richard Gideon with the El Codo Explosivo after a Hart Attack, with Zack Sirus counting the fall after a Diablo fireball had knocked out the referee.
matches.stipulation: Number-one contender match for the WFW World Heavyweight Title; both men agreed to no interference

matches.finish: Doc Silver escaped the cage to regain the World Heavyweight Title, crawling out from under the ring after he and Psycho fell through it; Green Machine had cut an opening in the cage and Scotty Michaels had struck Psycho's hand with a sledgehammer on the cage top.
matches.stipulation: Steel cage with razor wire on top and the door welded shut; Doc Silver added that a win could also come by escape
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: Posted in six parts after the first pay-per-view: a number-one-contender match, Felix Red's debut, and a steel-cage title rematch with razor wire on top and the door welded shut.

name: Scars and Stripes Forever

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Chris McMillan pinned Luster with the Dead Driver after a superkick and a kick to the midsection, after countering Luster's Funk and Wagnell with a back body drop.
matches.stipulation: Qualifying match for the North American Title number-one contender spot

matches.finish: Scotty Michaels pinned Tiny with the top-rope 360 legdrop after dodging a corner splash; Diablo had stood down from the match and named Tiny in his place.
matches.stipulation: Tiny's debut; the winner advanced to the number-one contender match for the North American Title at Paradise Lost

matches.finish: Rat Fink captured the American flag after his robot manager threw red pepper in Felix Red's eyes; when he lit a lighter to burn it, Felix Red kicked him down and raised the flag.
matches.stipulation: Capture the Flag: Rat Fink had to capture the American flag and Felix Red the Iraqi flag; the winner earned a title shot at Paradise Lost

matches.finish: Shawn Hart pinned both Richard Gideon and Doc Silver in one cover after clotheslining Psycho, who had snapped and chaired both of them, out of the ring; Hart won the right to name the stipulation for his title match and Gideon became his lackey for a month.
matches.stipulation: Ultimate Jeopardy tag team match, no time limit

matches.finish: Michael Manson kept the title with Sweet Dreams after braces on both knees, a low blow and a fireball that Diablo blew into Andre Eian's face while the referee was down.
matches.stipulation: North American Title match, one fall, sixty-minute time limit
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american

notes: Posted on 10 and 11 July 2003 in six parts (the tag match was posted after the main event but is played before it); the title of the first post is spelled "Scares and Stripes Forever." Copycat made his return, and the card set the contenders for Paradise Lost.

name: Paradise Lost

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Scotty Michaels rolled up Chris McMillan with a handful of tights with seven seconds left in the thirty-minute limit (told in the opening recap).
matches.stipulation: Number-one contender match for the North American Title, thirty-minute time limit

matches.finish: Copycat beat Ebony Jade in under a minute with the Kit Kat Kick and the Cat's Claw, after she had insulted him (told in the opening recap).
Southern Thunder pinned El Arco Iris with a flying clothesline after a spear, a bulldog and a long string of near-falls.
matches.stipulation: Southern Thunder's debut

matches.finish: Felix Red pinned Luster with the Shattered Horizon twisting swanton after a reverse DDT.
matches.stipulation: The winner met Rat Fink at the pay-per-view

matches.finish: Richard Gideon pinned Michael Manson with the System Failure after Scotty Michaels hit Manson with a chair behind the referee's back; afterwards Hart, Diablo, Michaels and Gideon beat Manson down until Felix Red ran in with a chair.
matches.stipulation: Handicap match (Andre Eian, Manson's partner, had been blinded by Diablo before the show)

matches.finish: Rat Fink was declared the winner by disqualification when Shawn Hart, Richard Gideon and Diablo ran in, handcuffed both men to the ropes and attacked; Doc Silver kept the title, and Manson saved the two men with a chair.
matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Title match
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: Posted in five parts from 25 to 27 July 2003. The opening post recounts two matches played before the cameras came on (Scotty Michaels over Chris McMillan at the thirty-minute mark, and Copycat over Ebony Jade) and carries Sean Edmunds' debut speech.

name: Spirit of NGEN

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Diablo won when Eian went over the top rope through a burning table off a back body drop; Eian, who had earlier put Diablo through two unlit tables, left the WFW as the stipulation required.
matches.stipulation: Flaming Tables match (the first man put through a flaming table wins); Andre Eian had to retire if he lost

matches.finish: Copycat made Southern Thunder submit to the Cat's Claw after Thunder missed a corner spear and separated his shoulder.
matches.stipulation: Number-one contender match for the North American Title

matches.finish: Felix Red pinned Rat Fink with the Shattered Horizon after a second referee was called in, with Fink's foot under the bottom rope.
Luster pinned Chris McMillan with the Funk and Wagnell powerbomb after kicking El Arco Iris over the top rope, ending his losing streak.
matches.stipulation: Three-way, single elimination

matches.finish: Sean Edmunds pinned Richard Gideon with a small package as Gideon set up the Final Judgment STF, after the referee had been knocked down twice.
matches.stipulation: Sean Edmunds' debut

matches.finish: Scotty Michaels pinned Michael Manson with the Viewer's Delight brainbuster after the lights went out and Luster, standing in the cage doorway with a pipe, struck Manson; Michaels became champion.
matches.stipulation: Steel cage match for the North American Title
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american

matches.finish: Shawn Hart won the lumberjack fall when Wylde stopped it as Doc Silver, blinded by a Diablo fireball, was held in a sleeper; Silver won the cage fall with the Aces Full; Hart won the Last Man Standing fall on the ten count and with it both the WFW and BAD World Heavyweight Titles.
matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Title match, best two out of three falls: a lumberjack match, a cage match and a Last Man Standing match, with Alex Wylde refereeing
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: Posted from 16 to 20 August 2003 in ten parts; the card's own date is Monday 11 August 2003, "Twelve Years and Going Strong." The introduction honours the old NGEN's alumni, and the title match is posted in three parts, one for each fall (the cage fall was posted last but is played second). Shawn Hart won both the WFW and BAD titles and handed the BAD title to Diablo.

name: NYC Unplugged

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Adam Benjamin pinned El Arco Iris with the Yours Truly 2K3 powerbomb into a sitout piledriver after targeting his injured shoulder.
matches.stipulation: Adam Benjamin's debut

matches.finish: Luster pinned Pulsar with the Funk and Wagnell powerbomb after Pulsar ran into his raised knee; Scotty Michaels and Heel at ringside had drawn the referee's attention earlier, letting Luster land a low blow.
matches.stipulation: Pulsar's debut

matches.finish: Rat Fink pinned Diablo with Falcon's Arrow after The American and Fink Bot (in a Redskins jersey) joined in against Diablo, and became BAD World Heavyweight Champion.
matches.stipulation: BAD World Heavyweight Title match, falls count anywhere, no disqualification, no countouts
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight

matches.finish: Alex Wylde struck his own partner Shawn Hart with a steel chair, Doc Silver covered the champion, and Silver and Michael Manson won; Wylde and Silver beat Hart down until Diablo made the save with a chair.
matches.stipulation: Tag team match; the winners met each other at Almost Live for a World Heavyweight Title shot

matches.finish: Jared Wells, in a black mask and trench coat, knocked Sean Edmunds out with a baseball bat while the referee was down, Richard Gideon locked on the Final Judgment, and the referee stopped the match.
matches.stipulation: The winners met each other for a North American Title shot at the pay-per-view

notes: A free show for New Yorkers who sat through the 2003 blackout, posted from 5 to 8 September 2003 in six parts; the tag match with Alex Wylde is told in a recap because it began during a commercial break, and the four-man match was moved to last after heated words between its men.

name: Almost Live

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Michael Manson pinned Doc Silver with Sweet Dreams, having become the first man to kick out of the Aces Full; Silver was suspended for ninety days.
matches.stipulation: Number-one contender match for the World Heavyweight Title; if Silver lost he was suspended for ninety days

matches.finish: El Arco Iris pinned Dormant after Scotty Michaels accidentally hit Dormant with the ring bell, for his first win in the WFW; Luster, Michaels and Heel then beat him down until Copycat made the save with a chair.
matches.stipulation: Dormant's debut

matches.finish: The referee ruled a draw at the thirty-minute mark although Gideon had Felix Red in the Final Judgment STF; Shawn Hart then announced that both men would face Scotty Michaels in a three-way for the title.
matches.stipulation: Number-one contender match for the North American Title, thirty-minute time limit

matches.finish: Rat Fink kept the title by pinning Psycho after hitting him in the back of the head with a Heinz ketchup bottle in a concession stand, with The American's help earlier in the brawl.
matches.stipulation: BAD World Heavyweight Title match, falls count anywhere, no disqualification, no countouts; Psycho's comeback after sixty days away
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight

matches.finish: Pulsar pinned Diablo with the Black Hole after Alex Wylde's top-rope Gatecrasher superkick, while Wylde tackled Jared Wells to stop him breaking up the fall; Jared Wells and Alex Wylde were making their ring debuts.
matches.stipulation: Six-man street fight; pinfalls count only inside the ring, no tagging

matches.finish: Scotty Michaels kept the title by pinning Copycat after hitting him with brass knuckles thrown in by Luster; Heel had chair-shotted Copycat and carried him backstage, and P. Nut, dressed as Copycat, lay on the mat for a count the referee refused.
matches.stipulation: North American Title match
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american

notes: The fed's version of Saturday Night's Main Event, posted from 26 to 30 September 2003 from the old BAD grounds in Revere. The lineup also billed Adam Benjamin against Demonite; no post for that match is among the threads held.

name: New World Madness

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: El Arco Iris pinned Adam Benjamin after hitting him with a loaded Care Bear (told in the opening recap).
matches.stipulation: Falls count anywhere through a children's hospital ward, played before the broadcast

matches.finish: Pulsar pinned Dormant with the Black Hole after Dormant had spiked him with a powerbomb on the floor, and earned the title shot at Ghoulish Games.
matches.stipulation: Number-one contender match for the BAD World Heavyweight Title

matches.finish: The referee called a double count-out at 29:57 with both men on the floor, Sensational Sherri hanging on to Copycat's foot and Edmunds pulling his other leg.
matches.stipulation: WWL bragging rights, thirty-minute time limit

matches.finish: Alex Wylde won when a masked man chair-shot Diablo and Wylde stun-gunned him face first through the burning crate; Diablo had earlier gone through the flaming table himself on a missed dive, which did not count.
matches.stipulation: Soap box against flaming table: Wylde had to put Diablo through the crate, Diablo had to put Wylde through a flaming table

matches.finish: Felix Red pinned Richard Gideon with the Ecstasy of Agony, a modified angle slam, while Psycho and Rat Fink brawled on the floor; Manson and Felix Red won the ban on Diablo, Tiny, Luster, P. Nut and Heel.
matches.stipulation: Ultimate Jeopardy three-way tag under BAD rules: Scotty Michaels and Rat Fink would pick their pay-per-view stipulations, Manson and Felix Red would ban Diablo, Tiny, Luster, P. Nut and Heel from ringside, and Gideon and Psycho would give Gideon his stipulation against Michaels and Psycho the first shot at the North American Champion

matches.finish: Shawn Hart kept the title with the El Codo Explosivo after Copycat and El Arco Iris interfered against Luster with chairs and a tornado DDT, stopping his Funk and Wagnall powerbomb; Manson attacked Hart afterwards.
matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Title match, Shawn Hart's first defence
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: Posted from 21 to 24 October 2003 in seven parts (the match with the mystery man was posted before his reveal), as the Columbus Day card. The opening post tells in a recap a falls-count-anywhere match between El Arco Iris and Adam Benjamin played earlier in a children's hospital, and announces that the GLCW has closed. The fed's promos for the card are on its roleplay pages.

name: Ghoulish Games

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Psycho pinned Dormant with the Tiger Driver after Dormant drove his own shoulder into the ring post with a spear.
matches.stipulation: Dormant's pay-per-view debut in his home town

matches.finish: Rat Fink kept the title: The American threw him a Green Bay Packers helmet, he headbutted Pulsar with it, took the loaded glove and punched a chair that Satan's Clause held in Pulsar's face, then pinned him.
matches.stipulation: BAD World Heavyweight Title match under BAD rules: guest spinner Andy Dick landed the wheel on a Coal Miner's Glove match
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight

matches.finish: Minion pinned Adam Benjamin after a T-bone suplex on his neck and a powerbomb onto the exposed metal turnbuckle.
matches.stipulation: Minion's WFW debut

matches.finish: Copycat pinned Luster with the Litterbomb with El Arco Iris lying across him, after El Arco Iris felled Edmunds with the Happy Dance kick; Sensational Sherri's gift box, opened by El Arco Iris, held two dead blue jays.
matches.stipulation: Double dog collar tornado match: the referee strapped El Arco Iris to Sean Edmunds and Copycat to Luster, and the first pinfall on a member of the other team won

matches.finish: Alex Wylde pinned Good Eddie, hooking his trunks, with the Gatecrasher superkick after Eddie had worked over his back and Wylde had fought back with a standing dropkick and a rocker dropper.
matches.stipulation: Good Eddie's debut

matches.finish: Anarky pinned Diablo (billed Ultimo Diablo) with a flying elbow drop off the shed ladder that drove an unfinished tombstone into his face, after Diablo's superfly splash had burst bags of fertilizer over both men.
matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere in the Graveyard, a Halloween match the commentators trace back thirteen years; falls counted only in the cemetery; Anarky's debut

matches.finish: Scotty Michaels passed out in Richard Gideon's figure-four leglock and the referee called the bell, making Gideon champion; Michaels' cousin Shawn Matthews had hit his bad leg with a chair and Felix Red had hurt his own leg on a missed swanton.
matches.stipulation: North American Title three-way
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american

matches.finish: Shawn Hart kept the title with an El Codo Explosivo after pretending to be blinded by Manson's yellow mist; Scotty Michaels and Terrell Mason had interfered against Manson, and Anarky raised Manson's arm afterwards.
matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Title, Chicago street fight; Diablo and Tiny were barred from ringside on pain of ninety days' suspension
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: The fed's Halloween pay-per-view, posted from 15 to 19 November 2003 in nine parts. Manson's challenge to Shawn Hart was a Chicago street fight; the graveyard match is a Halloween tradition the commentators trace to the old NGEN.

name: Turkey Day Terror

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Luster pinned Shawn Hart with the Funk and Wagnall powerbomb after Pulsar's Black Hole and Dormant's cluster, once Good Eddie had walked out and Terrell Mason had hit Hart with the Clap Back and left.
matches.stipulation: Six-man tag match

matches.finish: El Arco Iris pinned Minion with the Happy Dance kick after Shawn Hart's chair shot and El Codo Explosivo had not put him down; Minion clotheslined both men over the top rope afterwards.

Felix Red pinned Rat Fink with Ecstasy Through Agony through the table after two fans, Toxick White and Krist Blue, ran in against Fink's men and blinded Fink with powder; Felix Red told them to leave.
matches.stipulation: BAD World Heavyweight Title match under BAD rules
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight

matches.finish: The referee declared a double disqualification after Anarky beat Manson with a police nightstick before the bell, Manson cut Anarky's forehead with a police star and the two fought into the crowd until a riot and police with drawn guns ended it.

Alex Wylde was eliminated first when Edmunds fell across him and Scotty Michaels and Copycat held Edmunds down for the count; Michaels pinned Copycat with the brainbuster, and Sean Edmunds won by pinning Michaels with the Northern Lights suplex, earning the World Heavyweight Title shot.
matches.stipulation: Four-way elimination match: the first man eliminated would get a North American Title shot at a house show, the second a North American Title shot at the pay-per-view, the third a World Heavyweight Title shot at a house show and the winner a World Heavyweight Title shot at the pay-per-view

matches.finish: Richard Gideon kept the title when the referee disqualified Psycho for jabbing him in the forehead with a fork; Psycho then rammed the fork into the referee's head.
matches.stipulation: North American Title match
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american

notes: The fed's Thanksgiving card, posted from 8 to 13 December 2003 in seven parts. The Manson-Anarky match ended in a riot and the two were barred from facing each other; the four-way elimination match set the World Heavyweight Title shots for the next two cards.

name: Merrython

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Larry Tact made Pulsar pass out in the Skylock Inverted STF, and the referee called the bell at 18:06.
matches.stipulation: Larry Tact's WFW debut

matches.finish: Richard Gideon pinned Satan's Clause with the System Failure frog splash off Felix Red's shoulders; afterwards Rat Fink locked the cage and Psycho threw a fireball at Gideon, broke Fink's cast over his head and hit him with the Tiger Driver.
matches.stipulation: No Rope Barbed Wire Cage Street Fight Tornado Death Match under BAD rules, the first of its kind in the fed (taken from a 1995 AAA match); Satan's Clause took Rat Fink's place by President Wylde's edict after Fink handed the referee a note about a leg injury

matches.finish: Copycat pinned Anarky with the Litterbomb after the bag Anarky had taken from Icekold exploded in a paint bomb and blinded him; Anarky had tasered Icekold at ringside and beaten Copycat's left foot with a baseball bat.
matches.stipulation: Santa's Sack O Weapons: each man brought a sack of weapons to the ring, no disqualification

matches.finish: Michael Manson pinned Terrell Mason with Sweet Dreams after El Arco Iris hit Mason with a loaded Funshine Care Bear and Good Eddie put out Minion's flaming barbed-wire bat with a fire extinguisher; Luster had not come in to save Minion.
matches.stipulation: Santa's Surprise match: presents containing weapons surrounded the ring

matches.finish: Alex Wylde pinned Jared Wells when a 25-foot Christmas tree fell behind Sean Edmunds, who was going to break up the cover; Sensational Sherri had broken a mirror over Wells' head, and Copycat, who hit Edmunds with the Kit Kat Kick afterwards, was thought to have pushed the tree.
matches.stipulation: Falls count anywhere in FAO Schwartz, no ring introductions

matches.finish: Scotty Michaels pinned Shawn Hart after Minion had hit Michaels with a chair and the wheelchair-using 'Steve Matthews' had jumped up, hit Hart with the wheelchair and laid Michaels across him; Luster proved to be the man in the movie mask, and Michaels said afterwards that the brother and his drunken act were a set-up.
matches.stipulation: Winter Wonderland match in Central Park, no ring introductions
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: The fed's Christmas card, broadcast from Rockefeller Center, FAO Schwartz and Central Park, posted from 30 December 2003 to 2 January 2004. The card's matches are told on this fed's pages in the order of the broadcast: Larry Tact against Pulsar and the No Rope Barbed Wire Cage Street Fight Tornado Death Match, then Anarky against Copycat, the Santa's Surprise six-man, the falls-count-anywhere three-way in FAO Schwartz and, in Central Park, Shawn Hart's World Heavyweight Title defence against Scotty Michaels. The fed's own list of its champions dates the title change to 31 December 2003.

name: Mind Over Matter

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Good Eddie pinned Mike McGee with the Last Prayer Pedigree after lariating Pulsar over the top rope; Pulsar had been gutwrench-suplexed onto the front-row chairs by McGee.
matches.stipulation: Three-way match

matches.finish: Felix Red kept the title when Psycho passed out in his sleeper and the referee called the bell; Richard Gideon had hit Psycho with a chain-wrapped fist and choked him with the chain before the bell, and Felix Red loaded his boot with it. Psycho wrote 'Gideon, you'll pay' on the mat in his own blood.
matches.stipulation: BAD World Heavyweight Title match
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight

matches.finish: Sean Edmunds pinned Larry Tact with the Northern Lights suplex after Sherri had twice stopped Tact, once with a loaded purse and once when Edmunds grabbed her hand to reach the ropes; Edmunds kicked Tact after a handshake until Copycat and El Arco Iris ran in with chairs.
matches.stipulation: A good old fashioned wrestling match; Larry Tact had asked that Sensational Sherri be banned from ringside and President Wylde refused

matches.finish: Rat Fink pinned Michael Manson after a flying headbutt, wearing Yalebot's Yale football helmet, onto Minion, who was covering Manson after powerbombing him into an exposed turnbuckle.
matches.stipulation: Bare Buckles match: all four turnbuckle pads removed, the metal exposed

matches.finish: Jared Wells pinned Copycat with the Rage Bomb after the lights went out and a masked man stood over Copycat; Anarky had pushed over an 83-year-old birthday guest who was Icekold in disguise, and she had kicked him in the groin.
matches.stipulation: Three-team match; the winners would name the stipulation of their matches at the pay-per-view

matches.finish: Alex Wylde pinned Richard Gideon with the Gatecrasher superkick, after faking a collapse in Gideon's chicken wing, loading his boot and grabbing the dazed referee's collar to reach the ropes out of the Final Judgment STF.
matches.stipulation: Number-one contender's match for the World Heavyweight Title: the winner would challenge the champion after the pay-per-view

notes: The fed's January card, broadcast from Jadwin Gym on the Princeton University campus and posted from 22 to 29 January 2004 in eight parts, the last show before the Great Expectations pay-per-view. Jonathan Marx joined Brandon Jacobs and Vic Waters at the booth. The fed's line-up post (a separate page) lists the card; the promos for it are on the roleplay pages. The masked man who stood over Copycat in the three-team match is shown by the fed's later posts to be Psycho.

name: Great Expectations

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Michael Manson made Terrell Mason tap out to the Tourniquet after Mason had hit him with a chair before the bell and landed on his right shoulder missing a frog splash from a ladder.
Alex Wylde pinned Rat Fink with the Gatecrasher superkick after the referee had been knocked down by both men and Satan's Clause and Fink Bot (called Rally Monkeybot) had interfered.
Pulsar pinned the Mighty Impala with the Black Hole after Impala had worked over his injured right shoulder with an arm wringer, a hammerlock suplex into the steel steps and a chair dropkick.
Larry Tact pinned Luster with a sitting hook of both legs after Luster's sunset flip, out of Tact's leg-scissors sleeper hold.
Jared Wells pinned El Arco Iris with the Rage Bomb after a masked man tripped El Arco Iris as he went for a flying forearm.
Minion pinned Felix Red with the Fall From Grace off the rocks of the stadium fountain, after Minion had run through the outfield wall and Felix Red had cut his head with a Snapple bottle.
matches.stipulation: BAD World Heavyweight Title match, falls count anywhere in Edison Field under BAD rules; Good Eddie, booked in the three-way, did not wrestle
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight

matches.finish: Richard Gideon kept the title by pinning Psycho with the Buffalo Bomb after a masked man (Jared Wells, named in later posts) struck Copycat and Gideon with a chair, Icekold's pepper spray, meant for the masked man, hit Psycho and the referee was down.
matches.stipulation: North American Title match, three-way
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american

matches.finish: Diablo, wrestling in Mephisto's costume, pinned Anarky after the final explosion, when a second Mephisto from the crowd hit the two masked men, Jared Wells and Psycho, with a chair; Copycat, masked as Mephisto, had hit Anarky with a running powerbomb before the bell and been sent out.
matches.stipulation: Exploding Barbed Wire Death Match, billed as Anarky against Mephisto, forty-five minutes to the last explosion; Mike Randalls was special referee

matches.finish: Sean Edmunds won five falls to four, pinning Scotty Michaels with the Northern Lights suplex in the last seconds after Luster hit Michaels with a chair and Copycat, the referee, kicked him with the Kit Kat Kick.
matches.stipulation: Ironman match for the World Heavyweight Title: sixty minutes, the most falls wins; Copycat was the special referee
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: The fed's pay-per-view, live from Edison Field, posted from 18 to 25 February 2004 in eleven parts. The fed's own list of its World Heavyweight champions dates the Ironman change to 25 February 2004, the date of the post that tells it. A debut video for Iron Lion plays between matches.

name: Road to Glory

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Michael Manson won by pulling the feet from under Copycat and Jared Wells, the last two men, after Copycat had thrown out Anarky. Iron Lion threw out Pulsar and Ultimo Diablo, Psycho ran in with a chair to put Richard Gideon out, and El Arco Iris, with five men's help, eliminated Iron Lion.
matches.stipulation: So Cal Rumble: thirteen men entering every two and a half minutes, elimination by going over the top rope with both feet on the floor; the winner would challenge the World Heavyweight Champion at the Superbowl of Wrestling. Mephisto entered unannounced and Icekold entered the ring to save Copycat

matches.finish: Alex Wylde pinned Sean Edmunds with the Gatecrasher superkick after Edmunds, bleeding from the nose, lost his grip on the Northern Lights suplex; Sherri had hit Wylde with her purse and been sent to the back.
matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Title match
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: The fed's March card, live from Paradise Pier at Disney California Adventure, posted from 10 to 12 March 2004 in three parts: a thirteen-man So Cal Rumble, the winner of which challenged for the World Heavyweight Title at the Superbowl of Wrestling, and the World Heavyweight Title match. The fed's own list dates the Wylde change to 21 March 2004. Jonathan Marx was at the booth.

name: Vox Hiberionacum Part Deux

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Iron Lion pinned the Mighty Impala with the Pride Hammer, a stiff running powerbomb, after Impala had raked his eyes and fought from an armbar.

Scotty Michaels pinned Sean Edmunds by reversing his small package and hooking the ropes, after doctors in white coats had taken Luster away in a straitjacket on Michaels' tip and left Edmunds to face both men alone.
Pulsar pinned Michael Manson with the Black Hole right after Alex Wylde hit Manson with the Gatecrasher superkick; Mike McGee and the Mighty Impala had come to ringside to protect Wylde.
matches.stipulation: Tornado rules tag team street fight

matches.finish: El Arco Iris passed out under the boots of Anarky, Jared Wells, Psycho and Felix Red and the referee called the bell. Felix Red, entering last as Copycat's fourth man with Luster's shirt on his shoulder, had turned on Copycat's team with a spinning heel kick; the fourth man of Anarky's team had not come out, and the commentators took Felix Red's prop to mean he had taken Luster out before the match. Icekold had broken a beer bottle over Anarky's head as he entered, and Gideon had handcuffed Wells to the cage until Psycho took the key from Gideon's trunks and Anarky freed him. After the bell Anarky announced the Liars, Oppressors and Violence Experiment, L.O.V.E.
matches.stipulation: War Games: two rings in one cage, the teams alternating entries one man at a time every two minutes, won only by making a member of the other team submit or surrender once all eight were in; Richard Gideon's team lost the coin toss, so Jared Wells' team had the first advantage

notes: The fed's St. Patrick's Day card, live from Wonderland Park, posted from 27 March to 1 April 2004: its first six posts tell the Iron Lion, tag and street fight matches and the debut vignette of Alessandro Giovanni, and the post of 1 April tells the War Games main event, Anarky, Jared Wells, Psycho and a mystery man against Copycat, Richard Gideon, El Arco Iris and Felix Red, which launched L.O.V.E. Chris Wink, one of the four 'old men' on the board of directors, announced the line-up for the Superbowl of Wrestling at Gillette Stadium on this card; that card is told on the Superbowl of Wrestling show page.

name: Superbowl of Wrestling

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: El Arco Iris pinned Iron Lion with the Happy Dance after the referee, knocked down when Iris fell on him from Iron Lion's missile dropkick, had come round. Iron Lion had pinned Larry Tact earlier with the Pride Hammer, after El Arco Iris's missile dropkick to Tact.
matches.stipulation: Three-way elimination match

matches.finish: Shawn Hart's El Codo Explosivo left both men down after about forty minutes, and the referee reached ten on both and declared a double knockout; Scotty Michaels then went to attack Hart again, offered his hand instead, and Hart shook it.

Jared Wells threw Rat Fink over the side of a stadium ramp, swung a beer bottle at his hands until he lost his grip and fell into a garbage bin below, then jumped off the ramp onto him with the Alabama Jam from the Heavens and pinned him for the vacant title. Wells had pinned Pulsar earlier with a Rage Bomb into mirror shards in a bathroom, and Rat Fink had pinned Felix Red with a crucifix powerbomb through a metal door after Satan's Clause threw a roll of toilet paper at Red.
matches.stipulation: Four-man elimination falls count anywhere match for the vacated BAD World Heavyweight Title, fought through the stadium; the eight men announced were cut to four when Copycat attacked Good Eddie, the Mighty Impala, Alessandro Giovanni and the masked mystery man backstage
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight

matches.finish: Sean Edmunds pinned Jean Rabesque with the Northern Lights suplex in 44 minutes 50 seconds after hitting him twice with brass knuckles that Sensational Sherri had thrown from her cleavage; Edmunds slipped the knuckles into Rabesque's tights.

Copycat pinned Dan Ryan with the Litterbomb after Icekold climbed into the ring and, while the referee was ordering her out, Copycat kicked Ryan in the groin; Copycat then locked on the Cat's Claw until officials pulled him off.

Psycho won two falls to one. He took the first by making Gideon give up to a full nelson, Gideon took the second with a Tombstone piledriver into light tubes after a System Failure frog splash got two, and Psycho took the Texas Death Match when Gideon could not get up at the ten count; Gideon then handed Psycho the title, and Anarky, Jared Wells and Felix Red helped Psycho out.
matches.stipulation: Two out of three falls: the first fall submissions only (Gideon's pick), the second the Four Corners of Hell (Psycho's pick), the third a Texas Death Match
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american

matches.finish: Anarky pinned Maelstrom with the Chaos Breaker after Maelstrom had him in Mortal Sin; Anarky had shoved the referee, used a wrench and the cage platform. After the bell the lights went out and Scotty Michaels and a masked man attacked Anarky.
matches.stipulation: Double steel cage match

matches.finish: Michael Manson pulled Alex Wylde off the ladder; when Wylde pulled the ladder away, Manson hung from the belt fifteen feet up, lifted his legs over Wylde's swing with the folded ladder and dropped to the mat with the belt to become champion. Wylde had hurt his knee earlier.
matches.stipulation: Ladder match for the World Heavyweight Title with the belt hung fifteen feet above the ring; Joey Melton was the special referee, enlisted by the board of directors on Manson's behalf and to keep the match clean
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: The fed's anniversary card, live from Gillette Stadium, posted from 18 to 29 April 2004 in eleven parts (the North American Title match is three of them, one per fall), with talent from the WFW, GXE, the CSWA, NEW and the old GLCW. The fed's own lists of its champions date the North American change to 26 April 2004 and the World Heavyweight change to 29 April 2004, the days the posts telling those matches went up; the first post of the broadcast is dated 18 April 2004, which this record uses. Aaron Boone of the Yankees, in the masked mystery man's place, and the baseball manager Grady Little, who brought out the ladder, are real people staged in the fiction. Larry Tact is billed in the commentary as the NEW World Heavyweight Champion, and the figures given for Jean Rabesque's record against Edmunds disagree (17-0 in the opening commentary, 11-0 in the match commentary and in Edmunds' promo).

name: Shock & Awe II

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: The referee called for the bell at the twenty-minute limit and the ring announcer declared a time limit draw; Mike Lane had hit Michael Dice with the 1999 on the concrete and collapsed beside him while trying to roll him back into the ring.
matches.stipulation: Debut match, twenty-minute time limit

matches.finish: Sean Edmunds pinned Pulsar with the Northern Lights suplex, holding a handful of Pulsar's tights; earlier he had pulled the referee into Pulsar's charge at the turnbuckle and hit Pulsar with the purse Sensational Sherri threw him.

The referee disqualified Anarky and Jared Wells when Psycho, with Felix Red at ringside, hit Iron Lion in the back with a chair to break up a Pride Hammer pin on Wells; L.O.V.E. beat Iron Lion with chairs after the bell and Anarky hit him with a Chaos Breaker on a chair before Larry Tact ran in with a baseball bat.
matches.stipulation: Iron Lion alone against Anarky and Jared Wells

matches.finish: Copycat won with the Cat's Claw, Larry Tact out on his feet, and Edmunds, the special referee, was left to call for the bell; Edmunds, knocked down earlier when Copycat pushed him onto a banana peel, had come round and superkicked Tact by mistake when Copycat ducked. After the bell Copycat locked the Cat's Claw on the Mighty Impala.
matches.stipulation: Sean Edmunds was the special referee, with Mike McGee and the Mighty Impala at ringside

matches.finish: Felix Red pinned El Arco Iris with a spinning heel kick after a little girl from the crowd, in Felix Red's ruse, held a knife to the throat of a bunny rabbit and Iris broke his figure-four hold to plead with her; Gideon snatched the rabbit during the count, and Felix Red took the girl off through the crowd.
matches.stipulation: Three-way number-one contender's match

matches.finish: Rat Fink pinned Psycho with the crucifix powerbomb onto a pool table; Golem made his debut as Psycho's partner. After the bell Rat Fink stole Manson's van again.
matches.stipulation: Boot Camp match, falls count anywhere around the ringside area; Manson's black van crashed through the ring

notes: The fed's second Shock & Awe, live from the Pepsi Arena, posted from 18 to 23 May 2004 in ten parts; the first Shock & Awe was the card of April 2003. Jonathan Marx joined the booth after Brandon Jacobs was put through a table. The post of 22 May carrying the three-way match was captured only by Common Crawl.

name: BOMB Voyage

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Arquito Iris pinned PHENOMITO with the Triple Lindy after the referee was bumped.
matches.stipulation: Minis match

matches.finish: Iron Lion pinned Anarky with the Pride Hammer, a running powerbomb, after Anarky's running shoulder block; Anarky had come out in camouflage with a U.S. flag, and Iron Lion hurt his right knee.

Jared Wells kept the title: hanging from the railing after Mike Lane back body dropped him over it, he pulled Lane, wearing a life preserver, over the side into the water by its rope; after the bell Wells dropped the Alabama Jam from the railing onto Lane in the water. Lane had attacked Wells before the bell, the referee was cut by a chair shard, and Lane reached the match when Michael Dice was attacked before their rematch.
matches.stipulation: BAD World Heavyweight Title match under Wells Rules: the winner had to throw his opponent over the side of the ship into the water
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight

matches.finish: Larry Tact won with the Tactful Surrender and Sean Edmunds, his knee hurt when a fan pushed him over a speaker earlier, passed out and the referee called the bell; a woman billed as "Blue Lioness", whom the commentary once calls Sherri, had hit Tact with a loaded purse and distracted the referee until Tact punched her off the apron.
matches.stipulation: Sensational Sherri was banned from ringside

matches.finish: Pulsar pinned Felix Red with the Black Hole on the concrete by the pool; Golem hit Psycho with a chain after the bell.
matches.stipulation: Six-man falls count anywhere match around the ship

matches.finish: Michael Manson kept the title: with thirty seconds left he broke the Tourniquet as Richard Gideon neared the ropes, pulled him back to the center and locked it on again, and as the crowd counted the last seconds the referee checked on Gideon and called for the bell, and the ring announcer gave Manson the win at 59 minutes 59 seconds; Gideon had hurt himself on the System Failure. After the bell Jared Wells and Psycho attacked Manson, Wells Rage Bombed him through a flaming table, and Felix Red marked THE WORLD on him with a marker as Anarky wheeled in a birthday cake.
matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Title match, sixty-minute time limit
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: The fed's cruise-ship card, fought aboard the WFW cruise ship beside Honolulu and posted from 9 to 18 June 2004 in twelve parts; the promos for it were posted from 23 May. Jonathan Marx and Vic Waters called it while Brandon Jacobs, whose memory was gone after the table at Shock & Awe II, appeared only in a taped scene with his nurse below deck. It carried the fed's first minis match.

name: WWF Pandamonium

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Mike Lane pinned Zack Rosman in 2 minutes 3 seconds with his '1999' after attacking him before the bell.

Golem pinned Rat Fink, the last man, when Pulsar, already eliminated, pushed the blinded Golem onto him. Pulsar had been eliminated first, pinned beneath Rat Fink and a bookcase that Golem pushed over; Psycho, who was not in the match, was under the bookcase too, and the commentary says he cost Pulsar the match.
matches.stipulation: Three-way falls count anywhere elimination match through the zoo under BAD rules; the winner would get the first shot at the BAD World Heavyweight Title after the pay-per-view

matches.finish: Richard Gideon pinned Bartleby, in his debut, with a schoolboy roll-up from behind while Anarky, wheeling out a cake, distracted him; a stripper who popped out of the cake swung a crowbar at Bartleby.
Copycat made Jared Wells give up to the Cat's Claw, with Wells hung around the ring post, and the referee called the bell.
matches.stipulation: Double dog collar match: Copycat chained to Jared Wells and Iron Lion to Blue Cat by Sean Edmunds' edict

matches.finish: Anarky touched the fourth turnbuckle as Larry Tact's back gave out and he passed out.
matches.stipulation: Strap match: the winner had to touch all four turnbuckles in succession

matches.finish: Felix Red pinned Michael Manson with the Shattered Horizon from the top of the cage. After the bell Jared Wells, who cut the cage lock with hedge clippers, and Anarky beat down Manson and El Arco Iris, and Psycho tore Iris's mask off.
matches.stipulation: Cage match

notes: The fed's zoo card, live from the San Diego Zoo for the World Wildlife Fund and posted from 8 to 23 July 2004 in seven parts, the last show before the Cherry Blossom Chaos pay-per-view in Washington, D.C. Brandon Jacobs was back at the booth beside Jonathan Marx and Vic Waters, saying he still remembered little from the Superbowl of Wrestling on. Chris Wink announced the Cherry Blossom Chaos card after the main event.

name: Cherry Blossom Chaos II

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

venue: the National Mall, by the Reflecting Pool

matches.finish: Luster pinned one of several men in Bartleby's mask with a small package after the referee, thrown down earlier, came round, and the ring announcer gave him the match; a second Bartleby came from under the ring to protest that Luster had not pinned the real one, Luster Funk & Wagnall powerbombed two of them, and when he pulled the mask off the last the face was Shawn Hart's, who struck him with El Codo Explosivo after the bell.

Richard Gideon pinned John Doe in his debut with the System Failure, a 450 frog splash from the top rope, after working Doe's neck and back for most of the match; Doe had kicked out after the three brainbusters of the G-Clef and had missed a senton from the top rope.

The referee called for the disqualification of Mike Lane when he took a chair from an elderly woman at ringside and struck Golem in the face with it; Lane then put Golem down with a 1999 and choked the referee until security pulled him off. Golem had worked Lane's right shoulder for most of the match.

Scotty Michaels pinned Larry Tact with the Heartbreaker, a top-rope leg drop onto a steel chair, after Shawn Hart and El Segundo handcuffed Anarky to the guardrail and held Tact down, and Richard Gideon came over the barricade with a chair meant for Anarky that Tact took instead. Paramedics fitted Tact with a neck brace; Hart announced that the Fun Bus had joined forces with Michaels and Gideon.
matches.stipulation: Three-way dance, one fall to a finish

matches.finish: Copycat locked on the Cat's Claw, bleeding into his eyes, until Blue Cat passed out and the referee called the bell. Copycat had pulled the mask off on the top rope, and Blue Lioness threw her skirt in to hide his face, but Copycat pulled it away and the man was Sean Edmunds, who from the ropes after the bell promised Copycat the shot.
matches.stipulation: Copycat's World Heavyweight Title shot at the next pay-per-view if he won, as promised by President Edmunds

matches.finish: Jared Wells kept the BAD World Heavyweight Title with a Rage Bomb off the second rope for the three. Iron Lion's left knee, chop-blocked by Wells just before the bell while Anarky had Iron Lion's attention at the ramp with a cattle prod and an actress reading a charity appeal, gave out when Wells slipped off his shoulders as he ran for the Pride Hammer and he planted on it, and Wells set him on the top turnbuckle.
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight

matches.finish: Psycho kept the North American Title by pinning El Arco Iris, the last challenger, with the Psycho Flight off the lap of the Lincoln statue after Iris's shooting star press missed. Pulsar pinned Rat Fink first, and Iris pinned Pulsar after Rat Fink, already eliminated, hit Pulsar with a chair.
matches.stipulation: Falls Count Anywhere on the Mall II: four men, pinfall or submission to eliminate, fought through the Washington Monument, the Reflecting Pool and the Lincoln Memorial
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american

matches.finish: Michael Manson kept the World Heavyweight Title with a clothesline and a cover after Felix Red's flying spinning back kick missed. Manson had used low blows, a bottle and an umbrella; Red hit the Shattered Horizon in the rain, but the referee slipped and was slow to count and Manson kicked out.
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: The fed's second Cherry Blossom Chaos pay-per-view, staged on the National Mall and posted from 15 August to 3 September 2004 in ten parts: the introduction with the match-by-match preview, eight matches, and a video package for the Inner Circle that names nobody. Luster unmasked Bartleby as Shawn Hart in the first match; Copycat unmasked Blue Cat as the fed's President, Sean Edmunds, and won a World Heavyweight Title shot; the North American Title match, Falls Count Anywhere on the Mall II, ran through the Washington Monument, the Reflecting Pool and the Lincoln Memorial; rain fell on the main event. Anarky brought a real actress and a child out on the entrance way before the Wells-Iron Lion match as a diversion. Brandon Jacobs closes the show by announcing Paradise Lost at Fenway Park.

name: Paradise Lost

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: John Doe pinned Michael Dice with the Amnesia Attack at the twenty-one minute mark, having worn him down: Dice was back after being ambushed and put on the shelf by Shawn Hart at BOMB Voyage.
matches.stipulation: Dark match, told only in the news-desk recap

matches.finish: Pulsar pinned Rat Fink with the Black Hole at the seventeen minute mark after being busted open by an early chair shot and fighting Satan's Clause and Buckybot's interference; the two brawled through the crowd with a violin from a member of the Boston Symphony Orchestra, a bat that had belonged to Jim Rice and a kitchen sink.
matches.stipulation: Dark match under BAD rules, told only in the news-desk recap

matches.finish: Iron Lion pinned Sean Edmunds with a Yakuza kick after surviving a low blow ruse, a clipped knee, a half Boston crab and an elbow drop; he had hit the Pride Hammer earlier, and Sensational Sherri at ringside kissed the referee and held Iron Lion's bad leg.

El Arco Iris pinned Luster after his Happy Dance superkick and Felix Red's spinning heel kick caught Luster between them and knocked Red from the ring. Chris Wink then announced Guerra Interminable and named Iris the man to face Michael Manson there.
matches.stipulation: Three-way dance: the first pinfall or submission wins

matches.finish: Psycho kept the North American Title by pinning Golem after a Tiger Driver that Golem kicked out of and a moonsault that he turned into half a rotation, landing head first on Golem's ribs. Psycho had blinded Golem with thumbtacks, cut him open with a fork and struck the first referee with it, so the backup referee Umberto Gonzalez took over.
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american

matches.finish: Anarky pinned Michael Manson with the Chaos Breaker through a flaming table, winning for himself and Jared Wells; Mike Lane had set the bar on fire, and the teams had kept breaking up one another's covers. Wells had pulled a water gun on Lane to make him let go of Shawn Hart, and Manson told him to shoot. After the bell Felix Red and Psycho came through the front door and beat down Manson until Copycat came in with a baseball bat, took the title belt and dragged Manson out before the roof fell in.
matches.stipulation: Bar room brawl under BAD rules in a tavern across the street from Fenway Park, no entrances, the first pinfall winning the match for its team

matches.finish: Scotty Michaels pinned Copycat with the Heartbreaker from the top rope. Michaels then kept Copycat in the World Heavyweight Title three-way at Turkey Day Terror and named the match: a steel cage inside a steel cage, the cage that held Maelstrom and Anarky.
matches.stipulation: Lumberjack match with no disqualification, eight lumberjacks billed as MFL legends, Chris Wink among them: the winner could exclude his opponent from the World Heavyweight Title match or name its stipulation

notes: The fed's Fenway Park card, posted from 20 September to 9 October 2004 in ten parts. The second post tells, in a news-desk recap, three dark matches played before the broadcast (Striker over Man Beast with a roll-up from behind after Arquito Iris mooned Man Beast, then the two structured below) and the Mighty Impala's offer to Pulsar; the bar room brawl was fought in a tavern across the street and burned the tavern down; the steel cage for the main event was hijacked, so Chris Wink brought out eight lumberjacks billed as MFL legends, himself among them. The Inner Circle, Maelstrom, Dan Ryan, Christian Sands and their manager Lindsay Troy, arrive by limousine and sign. The ring announcer introduces the Edmunds-Iron Lion match as for the BAD World Heavyweight Title, a leftover line: no title changes hands. Chris Wink announces Guerra Interminable at Arena Mexico, and Brandon Jacobs closes with its card.

name: Guerra Interminable

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Team Anarky won with Anarky and Felix Red the survivors. The eliminations were Rat Fink (pinned by Thirteen's 13x13), Richard Gideon (John Doe's Amnesia Attack), Sean Edmunds (Rocko Daymon's Alabama Jam), Mike Lane (disqualified for a piledriver on Golem), Luster (Anarky's Chaos Breaker), Golem (Doe), Daymon (Anarky), Shawn Hart (Doe) and Doe (Thirteen), and Felix Red pinned Thirteen with the Shattered Horizon after Anarky hit Thirteen low and gave him a piledriver while Red kept the referee busy.
matches.stipulation: Torneo Cibernetico, two teams of seven under Lucha rules; the survivors of the winning team would face each other for a North American Title shot

matches.finish: Copycat pinned Scotty Michaels with the Kit Kat Kick. Psycho had opened Ryan's head with a fork, Ryan had answered with the Burning Hammer and a Humility Bomb on Michaels, and Psycho had chaired Ryan; Copycat blew mist into Michaels's eyes while Michaels held his arms for Psycho, and Psycho walked out on his partner before the pin.
matches.stipulation: Partners Incredible tag match under Lucha rules, Dan Ryan's WFW debut

matches.finish: The referee stopped the match with Jared Wells, already knocked out, in Maelstrom's Mortal Sin. They brawled through the crowd and ringside, where Maelstrom threw Wells three or four rows into the crowd and Wells speared him into the guardrail; Wells hit a top-rope leg drop and climbed to the top rope to Rage Bomb him, but Maelstrom locked on the Mortal Sin, Wells broke free and fell, knocking himself out on the ring steps, and Maelstrom rolled him in, locked on the Mortal Sin again and the referee called for the bell.
matches.stipulation: One fall under Boston Area Destruction rules, a non-title match, Maelstrom's WFW debut

matches.finish: Michael Manson kept the title two falls to one. El Arco Iris won the first fall with the Happy Dance after a Shining Wizard, Manson took the second with Sweet Dreams, and in the third Manson escaped Iris's Dragon Sleeper by biting his arm, beat him down with Wild Buck Bombs and, after a missed moonsault left Iris's shoulder hurt, locked on the Tourniquet and made him tap.
matches.stipulation: Two out of three falls under Lucha rules
matches.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight

notes: The fed's first show from Arena Mexico in Mexico City, posted from 3 to 21 November 2004 in eleven parts, under Lucha rules in which piledrivers and low blows are automatic disqualifications. Its parts also carry the presidential campaign: Lonestar, a masked candidate in a Republican nametag, stumps in the ring in the first part; the Mighty Impala shows Pulsar's sister on the family ranch in Australia on the video screen; Sebastian Dodd announces his signing in the ring in the seventh part. Maelstrom made his WFW debut against Jared Wells and Dan Ryan his in the Partners Incredible match. The fourteen-man Torneo Cibernetico was fought by twelve men: Pulsar left ringside after the Impala's video and the Impala never appeared. Chris Wink stripped the winners of the North American Title shot in the fifth part and set the Ghoulish Games card; the last part ends with Pulsar arrested at the airport.

name: Ghoulish Games

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Pulsar clotheslined Mike McGee before his entrance, threw him into the steel steps, rolled him into the ring and pinned him with the Black Hole, the bell ringing late; the match took two seconds.
matches.stipulation: One fall, the winner to face the Mighty Impala at the pay-per-view for Pulsar's sister

matches.finish: Sebastian Dodd pinned El Arco Iris with the D-ODDT, a DDT and Russian leg sweep combination, with both feet on the ropes for leverage after a low blow the referee did not see; he had put a foot on the ropes to break an earlier pin that the referee spotted. After the bell Iris hit Dodd and the referee with a chair and called Adam Benjamin, who ran to the ring to stop him, a traitor.
matches.stipulation: Sebastian Dodd's WFW debut

matches.finish: Cameron Cruise, masked as the Mystery Man, pinned Richard Gideon with Reality Check. Gideon led with three brainbusters and missed his System Failure, hurting his ribs; the special referee Joey Melton, who did not know who was under the mask, pulled it off himself while warning Gideon, caught in the Mystery Man's bear hug, not to grab it. Backstage Cruise rebuked Melton, who had signed a ten-show contract by mistake.
matches.stipulation: Special referee Joey Melton, named by President Edmunds; Cruise masked as the Mystery Man

matches.finish: Christian Sands pinned Mike Lane, who came to the ring drunk, with the Sandblaster after attacking him before the bell and working his neck with a reverse neckbreaker and a rolling neck snap. After the match Jean Rabesque came out and challenged the Inner Circle.
matches.stipulation: Christian Sands's WFW debut, with Lindsay Troy in his corner

matches.finish: Both men were counted out cold. Rocko Daymon landed the Brain Rocker Redux on the concrete and kicked John Doe off the apron at nineteen; Doe rose, hit the Amnesia Attack and then fell unconscious before covering, and the referee declared a double knockout. Chris Wink made Psycho's title match a Christmas Surprise match against both men.
matches.stipulation: Singles match, cut down from the Four Faces of Fear, for the right to meet Psycho for the North American Title

matches.finish: Sean Edmunds and Iron Lion won. Lonestar and Dick dragged Maelstrom into the crowd with a bullrope, Sensational Sherri jumped Dan Ryan and Edmunds chaired him, El Arco Iris carried Sherri off with Edmunds after him, and someone in a Laura Bush mask, Jared Wells in drag, chaired Ryan and dragged the unconscious Iron Lion over him for the three; Lindsay Troy pulled off the mask.
matches.stipulation: Tag match, cut down from a three-way with Luster and Rat Fink

matches.finish: Thirteen pinned Felix Red with the 13x13 frog splash, off a limousine, on his third dive of the match, after Red had kicked out twice. Thirteen had speared Red through a mausoleum wall; Red had caved in a bucket on Thirteen's head and opened him with a shovel. Felix Red then locked Thirteen in a casket and buried it in a fresh grave until officials arrived.
matches.stipulation: Falls count anywhere in the graveyard under BAD rules, the winner to earn a BAD World Heavyweight Title match

matches.finish: Anarky, Jared Wells and Psycho won. Each side pinned men in turn; Anarky hit Manson from a ladder with a flaming forearm and Psycho pinned him, but Scotty Michaels broke up the count, and when Psycho pinned Michaels after a Tiger Driver through a table Manson did not move and the referee reached ten.
matches.stipulation: Day of the Dead six-man tag, falls count anywhere with three referees: a pinned man also had to stay down for a ten count

notes: The fed's Chicago show, posted from 5 to 25 December 2004 in twelve parts, the last show before the pay-per-view. Sean Edmunds, slurring his words, fired the president-elect Felix Red in the ring and the owners rehired him by the end of the night; Chris Wink announced that a declaration left by Alex Wylde renamed the pay-per-view Christmas Card, so there was no Turkey Day Terror; El Arco Iris snapped backstage after losing and carried Sensational Sherri off during the Maelstrom and Dan Ryan tag; the three-way tag and the Four Faces of Fear match were cut down to a tag and a singles match; Lonestar and Dick attacked Michael Manson in the parking lot and Maelstrom in the crowd; Felix Red buried Thirteen alive; and Shane Southern came through the curtain at the end.

name: Christmas Card

date.source: The board's own post date of the broadcast's first part.

matches.finish: Jean Rabesque pinned Christian Sands with a fisherman suplex, hooking Sands's own damaged leg. Sands had worked over Rabesque's knee, Lindsay Troy had swung a chair at it and held his foot at the apron, Rabesque had got a foot on the ropes at one pin, and Sands had reversed Rabesque's figure four before the finish.
matches.stipulation: First match of a three-match series, Rabesque's WFW debut

matches.finish: Steve Johnson won, in his first match, by suplexing the Unnamed Bastard over the barrier. Johnson had sidestepped Luster's charge with a burning Christmas tree and drop-toeholded him over the barrier onto it, Akira's Ghost pinned Aaron Rage with the Holy Ghost Bomb, the Unnamed Bastard pinned Adam Benjamin and threw Akira's Ghost over the barrier, and Johnson, who had survived a bonfire of trees, hit him low before the throw. Mike Lane was a no show.
matches.stipulation: BAD Christmas Tree Lot Battle Royal, pinfalls count anywhere or a man is thrown past the barrier; the winner earned a BAD World Heavyweight Title shot

matches.finish: Pulsar won when the referee, who was checking on Pulsar in the Impala's crossface chicken wing, saw the Impala's shoulders on the mat and counted three; the Impala attacked the referee and Pulsar clotheslined him over the top rope and hugged his sister, freed from the cage.
matches.stipulation: Pulsar's sister suspended over the ring in a cage; if Pulsar won she would be freed

notes: The fed's Boston pay-per-view, renamed from Turkey Day Terror and posted from 18 January 2005; only its first nine parts fall in this slice, so the card here is partial and the double cage World Heavyweight Title match, the three-way tag, Sean Edmunds against Shawn Hart, Jared Wells against Thirteen and Psycho's Christmas Surprise match are told in later parts. The opening part says Scotty Michaels, attacked with a lead pipe outside his gym, may never wrestle again; later parts report attacks on Richard Gideon and Iron Lion. Felix Red, introduced as the new president, announced the fed's first World Tag Team Titles, to be won in an invitational tournament sanctioned by L.O.V.E.; Sean Edmunds, with a court order, claimed to remain president for the night.
